1. Purpose


The purpose of this procedure is to establish a systematic approach for maintaining all


facility assets, equipment, and infrastructure in safe and efficient working condition. It


ensures compliance with company standards and applicable regulatory requirements while


minimizing downtime and maintenance costs.


2. Scope


This procedure applies to all facility-related assets, including HVAC systems, lighting,


plumbing, electrical panels, and safety installations across all company premises.


It covers both
 
preventive
 
and
 
corrective
 
maintenance activities.


3. Responsibilities


●
 
Facility Manager:
 
Oversees implementation of maintenance plans and approves


maintenance schedules.


●
 
Maintenance Technicians:
 
Perform maintenance tasks as per this procedure and


document completion.


●
 
Safety Officer:
 
Ensures all maintenance work complies with safety regulations.


●
 
Document Controller:
 
Maintains updated records of maintenance logs, schedules,


and revisions.

1. Purpose


The purpose of this procedure is to establish a systematic approach for maintaining all


facility assets, equipment, and infrastructure in safe and efficient working condition. It


ensures compliance with company standards and applicable regulatory requirements while


minimizing downtime and maintenance costs.


2. Scope


This procedure applies to all facility-related assets, including HVAC systems, lighting,


plumbing, electrical panels, and safety installations across all company premises.


It covers both
 
preventive
 
and
 
corrective
 
maintenance activities.


3. Responsibilities


●
 
Facility Manager:
 
Oversees implementation of maintenance plans and approves


maintenance schedules.


●
 
Maintenance Technicians:
 
Perform maintenance tasks as per this procedure and


document completion.


●
 
Safety Officer:
 
Ensures all maintenance work complies with safety regulations.


●
 
Document Controller:
 
Maintains updated records of maintenance logs, schedules,


and revisions.


4. Definitions
●
 
Preventive Maintenance (PM):
 
Regular, scheduled maintenance to prevent


equipment failure.


●
 
Corrective Maintenance (CM):
 
Repair or replacement of equipment after a fault


occurs.


●
 
Work Order:
 
A formal document authorizing maintenance tasks.


5. Procedure


5.1 Preventive Maintenance


1.
 
Develop an annual preventive maintenance plan covering all critical assets.


2.
 
Assign maintenance intervals based on manufacturer recommendations or


equipment usage.


3.
 
Record all preventive tasks in the maintenance management system.


4.
 
Technicians perform the task, update checklists, and record findings.


5.
 
Supervisor reviews completion status and signs off.


5.2 Corrective Maintenance


1.
 
Any employee noticing a fault must raise a maintenance request through the DMS.


2.
 
The Facility Manager evaluates and prioritizes the request.


3.
 
Maintenance Technician diagnoses and performs necessary repairs.


4.
 
All corrective actions are documented and verified post-completion.


5.3 Safety Measures


●
 
Always isolate electrical power before repair work.


●
 
Use appropriate PPE (Personal Protective Equipment).


●
 
Ensure work areas are properly cordoned off during maintenance.


●
 
Follow Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures where applicable.
6. Records and Documentation


●
 
Preventive Maintenance Logs


●
 
Work Order Forms


●
 
Corrective Maintenance Reports


●
 
Equipment Calibration Certificates


●
 
Maintenance Schedule Register


All records shall be retained for
 
a minimum of five years
.


7. References


●
 
ISO 45001: Occupational Health & Safety Management Systems


●
 
ISO 9001: Quality Management Systems


●
 
Company Safety Policy


●
 
Equipment Manufacturer Manuals
